title: Insulation: What to Know and What It Pays
desc: Why insulation is often the best first upgrade, what to check before you hire, and every open insulation rebate we track, with the official page and date.
lead: Insulation keeps heat in during winter and out during summer. It is often the best first upgrade. Here is what pays today.
image_alt: Two workers in hard hats reviewing plans beside insulated wall framing
intro:
Insulation slows heat as it moves through your attic, walls and floors. A home that holds its heat can use a smaller heating system, and rooms feel steadier.

Many programs pay for insulation, and some tie it to a home energy assessment. That can mean an assessment before the work and another after. Others pay for an attic upgrade without one. The rules, and the starting insulation level they accept, are different in each place, so read the program page first.
checks: Do you need an assessment? Some programs need one before and after the work. Book it before any work starts.
Which parts of the house. Attics, walls, basements and crawl spaces often have different amounts.
Your starting level. Some programs pay only when the existing insulation is below a set level.
The contractor. Many programs need a participating or registered company.
The paperwork. Keep invoices and photos. Some programs ask for both.
faq: Should I insulate before getting a heat pump?
Often yes. Better insulation can mean a smaller system. Our guide on doing upgrades in order explains why.
In some programs, yes. In others, no. The table links to each official page.
Can condos or apartments get insulation rebates?
Many programs are written for houses. Check the official page for your home type.
How long do I have to apply?
It varies. Some give months after the invoice and some close on a date.
